description: Fig. 10 is a four-panel composite of bar-chart histograms, all sharing the same axes: y = "Precipitation hardening (MPa)" from 0 to 40 in 5 MPa steps, x = "Precipitate radius (nm)" from 0.5 to 5.0 in 0.5 nm steps, over a green-to-orange background gradient. (a) 3Cr: a red dotted vertical line near 1.0 nm separates the left field labelled σ_order from the right field labelled σ_coh+σ_mod; green σ_order bars span roughly 0.5–1.0 nm with the tallest approaching the 15 MPa gridline, and orange σ_coh+σ_mod bars span roughly 1.0–2.3 nm with the tallest near 15 MPa. (b) 2Ni: legend lists only σ_coh+σ_mod; no green bars and no red line; orange bars appear only above ~2.0 nm, with a gap between roughly 2.9 and 3.7 nm, and the tallest bars near 4.0–4.8 nm approach 40 MPa. (c) 2Ni3Cr: legend lists only σ_coh+σ_mod; a dense orange cluster spans ~1.5–2.6 nm peaking near 23 MPa, plus two isolated taller bars near 3.6 and 3.9 nm reaching about 27 and 29 MPa. (d) 2Ni5Cr: both legend entries and a red dotted line near 1.0 nm; small green σ_order bars reach only ~4 MPa, orange bars span 1.0–2.4 nm with a peak near 19 MPa, and one isolated bar near 3.1 nm reaches ~21 MPa. The group shows size-resolved contributions of the two strengthening mechanisms: σ_coh+σ_mod dominates in all four steels, while σ_order remains non-negligible only in 3Cr and 2Ni5Cr.

observations.observation: All four panels share the y-axis label 'Precipitation hardening (MPa)' (0–40, 5 MPa steps) and the x-axis label 'Precipitate radius (nm)' (0.5–5.0, 0.5 nm steps).

Panel (a) (3Cr) legend contains both σ_order (green) and σ_coh+σ_mod (orange), and a red dotted vertical line near 1.0 nm marks the boundary between the σ_order field (left) and the σ_coh+σ_mod field (right).
In panel (a) green σ_order bars occur only to the left of the red dotted line (radius below ~1.0 nm) and orange σ_coh+σ_mod bars only to its right.
Panel (b) (2Ni) legend lists only σ_coh+σ_mod (orange); no green σ_order bars and no red transition line are visible, and the orange bars begin at a radius above 2.0 nm.
Panel (b) orange bars show a gap with no bars between roughly 2.9 nm and 3.7 nm, then rise steeply to the tallest bars near 4.0–4.8 nm approaching the 40 MPa gridline.

Panel (c) (2Ni3Cr) legend lists only σ_coh+σ_mod; the histogram has a dense cluster between ~1.5 and 2.6 nm peaking near 23 MPa plus two isolated bars near 3.6 and 3.9 nm that are taller than the cluster.
Panel (d) (2Ni5Cr) carries both legend entries and a red dotted transition line near 1.0 nm, but its green σ_order bars are small, reaching only about the 4 MPa level.

The caption identifies the four panels as the 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr steels, and states the figure shows precipitation hardening at each precipitate radius according to the precipitate size distribution.
The citing text states that the red dashed line represents the transition radius at which the dominant strengthening mechanism shifts from σ_order to σ_coh+σ_mod.
The citing text states that for the 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr steels the strength contribution of σ_coh+σ_mod is dominant.
The citing text states that in the 3Cr and 2Ni5Cr samples, which contain LRO nanodomains, σ_order also contributes to σ_prep because some nanodomains are smaller than the critical size.

The citing text states that σ_prep is taken as the larger of σ_order and σ_coh+σ_mod, and that yield strength is predicted from the size distribution and volume fraction of κ-carbides and compared with tensile test results.

A red dotted vertical line near 1.0 nm marks the σ_order / σ_coh+σ_mod boundary, with shaded green and orange field labels.

Bar histogram for 2Ni3Cr steel. Legend lists only σ_coh+σ_mod (orange). A dense cluster of bars spans ~1.5–2.6 nm peaking near 23 MPa, with two isolated, taller bars near 3.6 and 3.9 nm reaching about 27 and 29 MPa.

Bar histogram for 2Ni5Cr steel. Both legend entries present (σ_order green, σ_coh+σ_mod orange) with a red dotted transition line near 1.0 nm. Small green σ_order bars reach about 4 MPa; orange bars span 1.0–2.4 nm peaking near 19 MPa, plus one isolated orange bar near 3.1 nm at about 21 MPa.
